1.4

Objects that belong

Build a sustained related series

Create a sustained body of related artworks in response to an art making proposition

Suggested teaching time
8–10 weeks

Timing, task steps and quantities are classroom suggestions, not NZQA grade requirements.

Read the standard (PDF)

The brief

Everyday objects can tell a story about belonging.

Respond to this starting proposition, or negotiate your own: everyday objects can tell a story about belonging. Develop a related series of paintings in which personal objects, pictorial relationships and paint handling work together. Select and order the finished works so the proposition is clear.

Materials & preparation

Personally meaningful objects, observational drawing materials, your own photographs, water-based paint, suitable paper or board, and materials for the approved portfolio format.

Use your own drawings and photographs as starting points. Record sources and seek permission for people, places and culturally significant material. Discuss tikanga and context with your teacher where relevant.

This is an external standard. Use the activities as teaching suggestions; make your own decisions during assessed work. Your teacher must keep support within NZQA’s annual conditions.

Suggested size & quantity

Use these ranges to plan your studio time and materials with your teacher. They are classroom suggestions, not NZQA minimums, maximums or grade requirements. Adapt them to your idea, working pace and access needs.

Finished series

A useful starting plan is 3–5 related finished paintings, mainly A5–A4. Vary the scale when it serves the proposition. Negotiate a different number if the complexity or scale warrants it; each work should contribute to the series.

Supporting studies

Try about 8–12 A6–A5 observational, composition and paint studies before and between the finished works. Use them to investigate relationships and solve problems as the series develops.

Workbook & presentation

Allow about 6–8 A3 workbook pages, or 12–16 A4 pages, for the supporting studies, sources and decisions. For the painting route, trial the finished works together on a full-size paper mock-up of the panel specified below before choosing supports. Keep room between works; the workbook is preparation rather than an extra submitted panel.

One workbook page means one side of a sheet; a two-page spread counts as two pages. A3 is 297 × 420 mm, A4 is 210 × 297 mm, A5 is 148 × 210 mm and A6 is 105 × 148 mm. Two A4 pages offer about the same area as one A3 page for planning; this does not change any external submission format. Mount small studies or use clear photographs of separate works rather than making everything twice.

Artist connections

Choose the connections that serve your intention. The contemporary models offer different approaches; select a relevant comparison rather than studying every artist. These works are references, not assessment exemplars.

Investigate how objects and their relationships can communicate belonging. Develop a consistent personal proposition across the series, using the artists as different ways into the question.

  • Ayesha Green

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Green’s flattened colour and still-life subjects open questions about representation, whenua and national identity. Read the context before comparing how an object can carry a public story and a personal association.

    McCahon House · Still Life education resource (PDF) · Painting investigation

  • Dame Robin White

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Use the gallery profile to investigate White’s relationship to people, places and collaboration. Look for clear shapes and intentional relationships between figure and setting; transfer a pictorial method to your own subject.

    Auckland Art Gallery · artist profile

  • Lubaina Himid

    Contemporary · Tanzania / United Kingdom

    Himid’s 2026 paintings explore belonging and making a home through figures and imagined settings. Study how relationships between people, painted space and everyday activity can carry questions about identity and place.

    British Council · 2026 British Pavilion guide (PDF) · Painting investigation

  • Frances Hodgkins

    Aotearoa New Zealand / Britain

    Look at how still-life objects and landscape can share a painted space. Try shifting the relationship between an object, its surroundings and its colour.

    Christchurch Art Gallery · Still Life

Studio sequence

Use this as a flexible route through the learning. Let the work suggest the next move.

  1. Make the proposition yours

    Choose objects you know well. Draw and photograph them yourself, and identify what they suggest about belonging. Rewrite the starting proposition in a way that reflects your own interest.

  2. Generate a family of possibilities

    Explore objects together and apart. Test cropping, viewpoint, negative space and palette in small painted studies. Investigate a relevant artist method using your own imagery.

  3. Develop related works

    Follow a promising relationship into further paintings. Let each work respond to a decision in the previous one, rather than repeat the same arrangement. Keep links through subject, process or composition.

  4. Strengthen the series

    Compare works together. Identify which choices support your proposition and which weaken it. Revisit a problem in a fresh work, aiming for increasingly consistent and skilful paint handling.

  5. Edit, order and finish

    Select the works that form a clear, finished series. Trial more than one order. Resolve the chosen works and curate the portfolio so thematic, stylistic and technical relationships are visible.

A useful studio conversation

Put two related works side by side. Describe what changed, show the evidence and explain what you will investigate next. Invite feedback, then make your own decision.

0 of 3 evidence checks complete

Presentation & submission

The 2026 painting route is one landscape A1 panel, photographed for digital submission. The alternative moving-image route is limited to 60 seconds. Your teacher manages school grading and NZQA verification. Choose the format with your teacher before making the final work.

Read the full 2026 NZQA specifications (PDF) and external assessment conditions. These are year-specific requirements; confirm any updates for your assessment year.

What changes between grades?

Student-friendly guidance adapted from the standard. The whole body of relevant evidence determines the grade; the examples below illustrate possibilities.

Grade distinctions for AS91915
GradeWhat the evidence needs to show
AchievementDevelop connected works that respond to a proposition using relevant art-making processes.In this task: The series has an identifiable subject or intention and visible relationships.
MeritSelect a cohesive group and maintain consistency in materials and techniques.In this task: The edited works belong together and the paint handling remains controlled.
ExcellenceClarify the proposition through the series while using processes and techniques skilfully.In this task: Each selected work helps the idea become clearer, supported by fluent paint handling.

Authority: NZQA AS91915 achievement criteria and explanatory notes (PDF).

Watch for

A group of unrelated best paintings does not communicate a sustained proposition.

Pause & reflect

If one painting were removed, what would the series lose? Use that question to test whether each selected work contributes.

Planning, assessment & differentiation

Keep this evidence focus separate from 1.3: this standard concerns a finished related body, while 1.3 concerns development and experimentation. If teaching is integrated, retain distinct evidence and judgements for each. Do not prescribe identical outcomes, a fixed number of paintings or a compulsory stylistic formula.

Support and stretch

For teaching practice, reduce the number of simultaneous choices, model one material process and invite oral discussion alongside drawing. Offer vocabulary prompts and accessible media. To extend the learning, ask students to compare alternatives, justify a rejection or investigate a consequence of their own decision. Adapt assessed support to the standard’s conditions and any approved arrangements.

Before issuing the task

Set local start and finish dates, agree available materials and check the current standard, conditions and exemplars. Use school authenticity processes and your normal moderation procedures. Adjust this brief to the class and context; it has not been quality assured by NZQA.
